tasks.short: Set priorities for the HR team and help people resolve difficult work.

today.trigger: Daily requests, team meetings and issues escalated by managers or HR colleagues.
steps: Review requests, deadlines and outstanding work across the 13-person HR team.
Check recruitment, payroll, absence and employee relations updates with the responsible specialists.
Set priorities and assign work across Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo.
Coach colleagues, resolve disagreements and make decisions on escalated issues.
Follow up on commitments and explain changes to site managers.
drudgery: Asking several people for the same status update.
Rebuilding action lists from meetings and email.
Checking whether owners have completed promised actions.
today.time_sinks: Assumed current workflow: updates are scattered across systems and conversations, so meeting preparation and follow-up consume time that could go into coaching.

lenses.faster: Compile a source-linked briefing of deadlines, workload and unresolved actions before the daily check-in. Draft action notes for review, removing repeated status collection and transcription.
lenses.autonomous: A scheduled workflow assembles updates and reminds action owners about agreed deadlines. Priority changes, sensitive escalations and allocation of people remain with the director.
lenses.ambitious: Give every site a weekly view of obstacles to getting new hires productive and retained through day 90. Use the saved preparation time to coach managers and remove recurring obstacles.
lenses.joy: Remove status chasing and repeated note-taking. Keep the conversations where the director helps colleagues make a difficult judgment or develop their skills.
lenses.options: Compare several ways to allocate HR capacity when recruitment peaks, absence cases and payroll deadlines compete. Show the consequences for service levels and the North Star.
lenses.altitude: Design the team's operating rhythm, escalation rules and service standards, then inspect exceptions and outcomes.
reach: Take on initial cross-site service analysis currently prepared by the People Analytics and HRIS Analyst.
Prepare capacity trade-offs with the Finance Director before requesting additional HR resources.

tasks.human_edge: Colleagues need a leader who understands workload, recognises conflict, builds trust and takes responsibility for priorities.
tasks.pattern_why: copilot: software can assemble the operating picture and draft follow-up, while leadership, coaching and judgments about people remain human.

in_practice.trigger: A scheduled morning briefing and preparation for the weekly HR team meeting.
steps: Read approved operational summaries and the shared HR action register using role-based access.
Calculate overdue actions and approaching deadlines with explicit rules.
Draft a briefing with source links, refresh times and conflicting information highlighted.
Let the director set priorities and confirm action owners during the meeting.
After review, record agreed actions and issue routine reminders.
in_practice.human_gate: The director confirms priorities, assignments and sensitive follow-up; generated summaries do not become employee performance assessments.
systems: Microsoft Teams, Outlook and restricted SharePoint
Read-only AFAS Profit, Recruitee and Studytube extracts
data_needed: Agreed action owners, deadlines and status definitions
Team capacity and availability
Operational service measures and escalation rules
Permissions separating routine work from confidential employee cases
in_practice.logs_to: A restricted SharePoint HR action register containing source links, approved actions and completion dates.

evidence.claim: SharePoint lists can hold shared action records with permissions and version history.
A source-linked briefing can reduce status collection, but its usefulness depends on consistent updates and access boundaries.
The 25% labour saving and 1.2 times end-to-end speedup are untested planning estimates.

risks: An incomplete briefing can hide urgent work or make one site's workload appear lighter.
Confidential employee relations or absence information could reach inappropriate recipients.
Turning task tracking into individual monitoring may require OR involvement and an EU AI Act assessment depending on intended use.
research_questions: How much of the director's time currently goes into status collection and follow-up rather than coaching or decisions?
Can the team maintain one action register without duplicating its existing work?
Does a four-week pilot reduce preparation time while preserving escalation quality and manager satisfaction?

tasks.short: Advise managers on HR policy and recommend changes when policies no longer work.

today.trigger: A manager asks how to handle a situation, or a case reveals a gap in policy.
steps: Clarify the facts, urgency and people involved.
Find the applicable policy, CAO provisions and approved guidance.
Discuss sensitive facts with the HR Business Partner or legal adviser where needed.
Explain the recommended action and document the advice.
Propose policy changes and arrange the required consultation or approval.
systems: Applicable CAO texts and legal reference sources
drudgery: Finding the current policy among old copies.
Answering repeated questions about the same rules.
Rewriting similar explanations for different managers.
today.time_sinks: Assumed current workflow: policy retrieval and first-draft advice repeat frequently; ambiguous facts, sensitive conversations and approvals take longer.

lenses.faster: Retrieve the applicable passages and produce a cited draft answer with missing facts listed. The director reviews the reasoning instead of searching and drafting from scratch.
lenses.autonomous: New questions enter a controlled queue that retrieves sources, drafts a response and flags sensitive topics. Advice is released after approval, with sensitive cases routed to the appropriate specialist.
lenses.ambitious: Provide consistent guidance for managers on every shift and at every site. Use recurring questions to identify policies that need clearer wording or better training.
lenses.joy: Remove repeated document searches and routine explanations. Preserve the careful conversations that help a manager respond fairly to a difficult situation.
lenses.options: Offer several lawful responses, explaining the employee impact, operational consequences and unresolved facts. Produce different wording for a manager briefing and an employee explanation.
lenses.altitude: Own the policy knowledge base, escalation boundaries and quality checks for manager advice.
reach: Handle first-draft policy queries that HR Business Partners currently prepare.
Give Learning and Development a prioritised list of manager training needs.

tasks.human_edge: Harassment, discrimination, dismissal and employee conflict require fair listening, contextual judgment and accountable advice; document retrieval cannot establish what happened.
tasks.pattern_why: agent_with_gate with an llm_step: retrieval and drafting can cover much of routine advice, but a person must approve its application to the facts. The earlier automate label fits preparation better than sensitive advice as a whole.

in_practice.trigger: A manager submits an HR policy question through an approved intake route.
steps: Collect the minimum necessary facts and identify the applicable employer entity, role and CAO.
Retrieve current approved policies and relevant source passages with effective dates.
Draft advice, identify missing facts and flag conflicts or sensitive issues.
Route the draft to the director, HR Business Partner or legal adviser for approval.
Release approved advice and record any proposed policy change separately.
in_practice.human_gate: An authorised HR reviewer approves every substantive response; harassment, discrimination, dismissal and legal uncertainty receive specialist review. Policy changes follow the applicable OR process before implementation.
systems: Restricted SharePoint policy library and advice register
AFAS Profit for necessary employment facts
data_needed: Versioned policies, owners and effective dates
Confirmed CAO applicability
Approved advice examples and escalation rules
Minimum case facts and access permissions
in_practice.logs_to: A restricted HR advice register recording sources, draft, reviewer, approved response and retention date.

evidence.claim: SharePoint supports versioned policy documents and permission-controlled libraries.
Retrieval from approved policies can support cited draft advice, but citations and applicability still require checking.
The 50% labour saving and 1.5 times end-to-end speedup are untested planning estimates.

risks: A convincing answer may cite an outdated provision or the wrong CAO.
Managers may treat a draft as binding advice or use it to prejudge a complaint.
Case intake may collect unnecessary personal or medical information, contrary to AVG data minimisation.
Employment decision support requires an intended-use assessment under the EU AI Act; meaningful human review must be maintained where required.
research_questions: What share of questions can be answered entirely from current approved policies?
Can reviewers reliably identify the applicable CAO and resolve conflicting sources?
On a blinded sample, do drafts match specialist advice without missing sensitive escalation triggers?
What OR, privacy and AI governance requirements apply to the proposed use?

tasks.short: Find the people problems behind the numbers and recommend what to change.

today.trigger: A monthly review, a worsening HR metric or a question from a site manager or the management team.
steps: Gather HR, recruitment, learning and agency data for the relevant period.
Reconcile definitions and compare sites, roles, shifts and cohorts.
Investigate unusual patterns with HR colleagues and managers.
Develop possible explanations and assess supporting evidence.
Recommend actions and agree how their results will be measured.
systems: Power BI on the nightly AFAS extract
drudgery: Reconciling employee and vacancy identifiers.
Rebuilding the same comparisons in Excel.
Writing commentary that repeats dashboard figures.
today.time_sinks: Assumed current workflow: data preparation and repeated comparisons dominate preparation; confirming causes requires discussions and operational evidence.

lenses.faster: Use governed calculations for recurring comparisons and draft commentary directly from checked tables. Remove manual reconciliation and chart rebuilding from each review.
lenses.autonomous: After the nightly refresh, run data checks and flag material changes against agreed thresholds. Produce a review pack that distinguishes observed changes from possible explanations.
lenses.ambitious: Evaluate whether onboarding, manager training and recruitment changes improve productive 90-day hires across all three sites. Include intervention costs and evidence strength in each recommendation.
lenses.joy: Remove spreadsheet assembly and repeated commentary. Keep the investigation with managers and the satisfaction of testing whether an improvement works.
lenses.options: Compare several explanations and interventions for the same pattern, such as shift scheduling, onboarding capacity or hiring delays. Show what evidence would distinguish them.
lenses.altitude: Set the company's people measurement standards and intervention evaluation method, then challenge conclusions rather than build every report.
reach: Prepare first-pass analyses normally requested from the People Analytics and HRIS Analyst.
Work with FP&A on the costs and benefits of retention and onboarding interventions.

tasks.human_edge: The director must challenge misleading comparisons, understand operational context and decide which interventions are fair and practical.
tasks.pattern_why: deterministic_software calculates and checks metrics; an llm_step drafts explanations; agent_with_gate keeps causal claims and recommendations subject to review.

in_practice.trigger: Completion of the nightly refresh, followed by the scheduled monthly people review.
steps: Join approved extracts using governed identifiers and check completeness, freshness and reconciliations.
Calculate agreed metrics using vacancy cohorts, 90-day observation windows, productivity checks and explicit agency-worker scope.
Flag material changes while suppressing small groups and showing uncertainty.
Draft findings with source tables, alternative explanations and evidence gaps.
Review findings with site managers and approve a measurable intervention.
in_practice.human_gate: The analyst validates calculations; the director approves interpretations and actions. Observational differences are not presented as proven causes or individual risk scores.
systems: Power BI and its governed data model
Read-only AFAS Profit, Recruitee and Studytube extracts
data_needed: Stable identifiers and agreed metric definitions
Vacancy opening, offer, start and leaving dates
Role-specific productivity confirmation and onboarding completion
Site, shift, contract type, aggregate absence and agency hours
Intervention dates, costs and relevant operational context
in_practice.logs_to: A restricted analysis register containing data versions, calculation definitions, findings, reviewer decisions and intervention results.

evidence.claim: Power BI supports reusable measures, scheduled refresh and row-level security.
Automated comparisons can identify patterns, but observational HR data alone does not establish their causes.
The 55% labour saving and two times end-to-end speedup are untested planning estimates.

risks: Immature 90-day cohorts, unfilled vacancies or agency workers may be excluded in ways that inflate results.
Site and shift differences may reflect job mix or seasonality rather than HR performance.
Small groups can reveal individuals even when names are removed.
Individual employment or health predictions would require a separate AVG and EU AI Act assessment; they are outside this workflow.
research_questions: Can vacancies, hires and productivity confirmations be linked reliably, and how will immature cohorts be reported?
Which recurring analyses currently consume the most director and analyst time?
Do historical alerts reveal actionable issues beyond what managers already know?
Can recommendations be tested with a credible comparison and sufficient sample size?

tasks.short: Run the HR programme across recruitment, training and labour relations.

today.trigger: The annual HR plan, monthly programme reviews or a major operational or labour relations change.
steps: Translate business priorities into HR programmes and intended outcomes.
Agree milestones, owners, resources and dependencies across sites.
Coordinate recruitment, training, employee lifecycle and labour relations activities.
Review delivery, risks and results with specialists and site leaders.
Adjust the programme and arrange management or OR decisions where required.
drudgery: Combining several programme status reports.
Maintaining duplicate milestone lists.
Chasing dependencies between HR, operations and managers.
today.time_sinks: Assumed current workflow: programme reporting and coordination are fragmented. This task concerns the monthly and annual programme, while daily team supervision is covered separately.

lenses.faster: Maintain one programme register and generate the monthly review from current milestones and outcomes. Draft dependency warnings and decision papers from that register.
lenses.autonomous: Routine milestone checks, certificate expiry checks and owner reminders run on a schedule. Changes affecting priorities, labour relations or employee arrangements go to the director.
lenses.ambitious: Run an integrated vacancy-to-day-90 programme with training places, manager capacity and onboarding readiness visible together. Test improvements across sites instead of managing separate departmental targets.
lenses.joy: Remove repeated status packs and calendar chasing. Keep programme design, negotiation and collaboration with site leaders and the OR.
lenses.options: Compare programme sequences that favour speed, lower cost or lower operational disruption. Show how training capacity and consultation requirements affect each sequence.
lenses.altitude: Design the HR delivery system and its decision rules, then intervene when outcomes or dependencies depart from plan.
reach: Prepare cross-site training capacity proposals with Learning and Development.
Develop the people readiness part of operational change programmes with site leadership.

tasks.human_edge: The director builds commitment, negotiates competing priorities and maintains constructive labour relations when plans affect employees.
tasks.pattern_why: copilot supported by deterministic_software for milestones and reminders: programme administration is repeatable, while priorities, consultation and organisational change require leadership.

in_practice.trigger: Monthly programme review, a milestone change or a certificate expiry entering the agreed warning period.
steps: Read the programme register and approved recruitment, learning and HR summaries.
Check milestone dependencies, training capacity and mandatory certificate dates using explicit rules.
Draft a portfolio review showing outcome gaps, options and decisions needed.
Let the director agree changes with programme owners, site leaders and the OR where applicable.
Record approved milestones, communicate decisions and follow up on dependencies.
in_practice.human_gate: The director approves programme changes and employee-facing communications. Managers verify task eligibility and certificates; absence coordination uses permitted administrative information, not medical judgments.
systems: Read-only AFAS Profit and Recruitee summaries
data_needed: Programme objectives, owners, milestones and dependencies
Recruitment demand and onboarding capacity
Course places, certificate requirements and expiry dates
Approved absence process deadlines under Wet verbetering poortwachter
Consultation requirements and decision dates
in_practice.logs_to: A restricted SharePoint programme register with approved decisions, milestone history and links to formal consultation records.

evidence.claim: SharePoint lists can maintain programme records and versioned changes.
Combining milestones and dependencies can reduce reporting work, but does not remove consultation or negotiation time.
The 30% labour saving and 1.2 times end-to-end speedup are untested planning estimates.

risks: Automated status reporting may look complete while owners have not updated the underlying register.
A completion record may be mistaken for a valid certificate or operational authorisation.
Programme changes may bypass required OR advice or consent if consultation is treated as an optional milestone.
These savings overlap daily supervision unless the two activities are measured separately.
research_questions: Which programme reports and milestone lists can be replaced by one shared register?
Are certificate expiry dates and operational training requirements complete and reliable?
Does the programme review improve week-one onboarding and 90-day outcomes without increasing owners' reporting work?

tasks.short: Build the HR budget and explain where spending differs from plan.

today.trigger: Annual budgeting, a forecast update or the monthly finance close.
steps: Agree budget scope and assumptions with Finance and HR specialists.
Collect staffing, recruitment, training, employment terms and agency cost inputs.
Build the budget and compare options with available funding.
Reconcile actual spending and commitments against budget.
Explain variances and recommend corrective action.
systems: AFAS Profit payroll, general ledger and accounts payable
drudgery: Copying actuals into budget workbooks.
Reconciling agency invoices, accruals and payroll totals.
Rewriting standard variance commentary.
today.time_sinks: Assumed current workflow: reconciliation and workbook maintenance take time before the director can assess trade-offs; HR operating costs and company-wide personnel costs may have different owners.

lenses.faster: Populate a controlled budget model from reconciled actuals and approved assumptions. Draft variance explanations with supporting transactions and unresolved questions.
lenses.autonomous: After Finance closes the period, refresh actuals and flag material variances or missing accruals. Keep budget approval, journal posting and payments within existing controls.
lenses.ambitious: Maintain a rolling view of the cost of getting a productive hire to day 90, including recruitment, training and early turnover. Reallocate spending based on outcomes as well as budget consumption.
lenses.joy: Remove copying, formula repair and repetitive commentary. Keep the conversations about which investments improve staffing reliability and retention.
lenses.options: Compare base, peak-season and constrained-budget scenarios with explicit CAO, agency rate and hiring assumptions. Show cash timing separately from recognised expense.
lenses.altitude: Own the budget assumptions, investment priorities and variance thresholds rather than assembling each workbook.
reach: Prepare the first HR forecast and variance pack currently supported by FP&A.
Work with the Controller on agency accruals and the financial benefits of retention improvements.

tasks.human_edge: The director weighs employee outcomes and operational needs against cost, challenges assumptions and owns spending commitments.
tasks.pattern_why: deterministic_software maintains financial calculations and reconciliations; an llm_step drafts explanations; agent_with_gate requires approval of assumptions and the resulting budget.

in_practice.trigger: A closed accounting period or the start of an approved budget round.
steps: Import approved actuals, commitments and staffing assumptions into a versioned model.
Reconcile totals to AFAS and check cost-centre mappings, agency accruals and duplicate costs.
Calculate scenarios using approved rates, employer costs, shift allowances and CAO effective dates.
Draft variance commentary that separates verified drivers from questions for cost owners.
Obtain Finance validation and the director's approval before publishing the budget or forecast.
in_practice.human_gate: Finance validates accounting treatment and reconciliations; the director approves HR assumptions and spending proposals. Existing approval limits govern commitments, journals and payments.
systems: Read-only AFAS Profit financial and payroll extracts
data_needed: Budget scope, cost centres, account mappings and approval limits
Closed-period actuals, accruals and committed spending
Approved headcount, hiring and learning plans
CAO rates, employer charges, agency rates and effective dates
Rules distinguishing HR operating costs from total personnel costs
in_practice.logs_to: The restricted budget library with reconciled input snapshots, model versions, assumptions and approvals.

evidence.claim: Excel Power Query supports repeatable import and transformation of structured data.
Rule-based financial models can calculate scenarios reproducibly when inputs and accounting mappings are controlled.
The 45% labour saving and 1.6 times end-to-end speedup are untested planning estimates.

risks: Agency invoices, accruals and payroll costs may be counted twice or in different periods.
Outdated CAO rates or missing employer charges can understate costs.
Generated commentary may invent a reason for a variance when only the numerical difference is known.
Savings may be double-counted with FP&A or Controller work unless responsibilities are measured separately.
research_questions: Does this task cover the HR department budget, total personnel spending or both?
Can a pilot reproduce the last three closed periods and their reconciliations?
Which assumptions and variance explanations still require substantial manual investigation?
How much director time disappears after allowing for Finance review and model maintenance?

tasks.short: Track legal and CAO changes and work out what Noordhaven must do.

today.trigger: A legal publication, court decision, CAO update or scheduled review of employment developments.
steps: Review legislation, relevant decisions, CAO publications and specialist updates.
Check authority, publication status, effective dates and applicability to Noordhaven.
Compare changes with current policies, payroll rules and working practices.
Discuss uncertain implications with the relevant specialist or legal adviser.
Brief management and assign implementation actions.
systems: Official legislation and court publication sources
drudgery: Scanning several sources for the same development.
Separating proposals from adopted requirements.
Comparing long documents and drafting repetitive summaries.
today.time_sinks: Assumed current workflow: screening and comparison consume most preparation time; unusual legal interpretation and implementation decisions require specialist attention.

lenses.faster: Collect changes from an approved source list, remove duplicates and show cited differences from the previous version. Draft a short impact note with effective dates and open questions.
lenses.autonomous: A scheduled monitor produces a change queue when approved sources publish updates. Nothing becomes company policy or a payroll instruction until reviewed.
lenses.ambitious: Maintain a current obligations register linking each applicable requirement to an owner, affected process and evidence of implementation. Include the agency workforce where obligations apply.
lenses.joy: Remove broad scanning and repetitive document comparison. Keep the interpretation, specialist discussion and practical translation into workable arrangements.
lenses.options: Show implementation choices, deadlines and dependencies where the law or CAO allows discretion. Separate mandatory changes from policy choices and proposed legislation.
lenses.altitude: Own the legal change control process and its coverage, rather than personally scanning every publication.
reach: Prepare change briefings for Payroll and Compensation and Benefits.
Coordinate initial employment-law impact assessments with Finance and operations.

tasks.human_edge: The director remains accountable for applicability, practical consequences and when to obtain legal advice; a summary cannot resolve every conflict between sources.
tasks.pattern_why: agent_with_gate with llm_step document comparison: monitoring and first-pass impact notes are repeatable, while legal interpretation and implementation require approval.

in_practice.trigger: A scheduled source check detects a new publication or a changed CAO document.
steps: Retrieve permitted publications from the approved source register and preserve version metadata.
Compare versions and extract relevant passages, publication status and effective dates.
Draft an applicability assessment covering the relevant CAO, workforce and affected processes.
Route uncertain or material interpretations to the director and legal adviser.
After approval, create implementation actions and track evidence of completion.
in_practice.human_gate: The director approves applicability and actions; a qualified adviser reviews material legal uncertainty. Payroll configuration and policy changes follow their separate approval and OR requirements.
systems: Approved official and licensed legal sources
data_needed: Authoritative source list and access rights
Current and previous CAO versions with confirmed applicability
Relevant workforce categories and company policies
Process owners, implementation lead times and consultation requirements
A maintained list of topics including Wet verbetering poortwachter, AVG and relevant EU AI Act obligations
in_practice.logs_to: A restricted legal change register containing source snapshots, citations, review decisions, deadlines and implementation evidence.

evidence.claim: Document comparison and source-based extraction can reduce first-pass legal monitoring work, but do not establish legal correctness.
SharePoint supports versioned documents and tracked records suitable for an obligations register.
The 60% labour saving and 2.2 times end-to-end speedup are untested planning estimates.

risks: A missed source creates false confidence that all changes have been covered.
A proposal, non-final decision or fact-specific ruling may be presented as a general binding requirement.
The wrong CAO version or effective date may lead to incorrect implementation.
Access restrictions and licensing may prevent automated retrieval of some sources.
research_questions: Which authoritative and licensed sources provide adequate coverage for both CAOs and relevant employment obligations?
Can the monitor recover known material changes from the previous year without excessive irrelevant alerts?
Do legal reviewers agree with the extracted status, applicability and effective dates?
Can every approved material change be traced through to verified implementation?

tasks.short: Oversee job evaluation and make sure roles are classified fairly under the right CAO.

today.trigger: A new role, a substantial change in duties, a classification review or an employee challenge.
steps: Confirm actual duties and the applicable job evaluation method with managers and employees.
Gather role descriptions, organisational context and relevant benchmark roles.
Have Compensation and Benefits assess the role against the approved criteria.
Challenge inconsistencies and obtain specialist input where needed.
Approve the classification through the required process and explain the outcome.
systems: SharePoint job descriptions and evaluation records
AFAS Profit role and pay structures
drudgery: Comparing inconsistent job description formats.
Searching for comparable roles and past decisions.
Compiling evidence and panel papers.
today.time_sinks: Assumed current workflow: evidence assembly is repetitive; establishing actual duties and resolving disputed classifications remain substantial human work.

lenses.faster: Turn approved role documents into a consistent evidence pack mapped to the applicable criteria. Highlight missing evidence and differences from comparator roles before the review meeting.
lenses.autonomous: A role change starts completeness checks and prepares a review pack. No classification, salary or contract change is issued automatically.
lenses.ambitious: Review comparable roles across all three sites for inconsistent treatment and outdated descriptions. Establish a clearer explanation and challenge route for employees.
lenses.joy: Remove document formatting and comparator searches. Keep the discussion about real responsibilities, fairness and recognition of work.
lenses.options: Show alternative classifications only where the evidence supports them, identifying the criterion that changes the result. Compare genuine role redesign options without inflating descriptions.
lenses.altitude: Own the evaluation method, consistency checks and appeal process rather than assembling each evaluation file.
reach: Prepare first-pass evidence packs for Compensation and Benefits.
Work with HR Business Partners on consistent role design across sites.

tasks.human_edge: A fair evaluation requires understanding work as performed, hearing challenges and defending a decision under the applicable method.
tasks.pattern_why: copilot with an llm_step for evidence extraction: the model can organise role information, but qualified evaluators apply the method and determine the classification.

in_practice.trigger: An approved request to create, change or review a role.
steps: Identify the applicable CAO and evaluation method before collecting role evidence.
Extract duties and responsibilities from approved documents, with citations and missing facts.
Assemble comparator evidence and an evaluator worksheet without personal performance data.
Have Compensation and Benefits validate duties, apply the method and document the rationale.
Let the director or authorised panel approve the outcome and follow the required notification and challenge process.
in_practice.human_gate: Qualified evaluators determine the classification and an authorised person approves it; the workflow cannot update pay or contracts. Applicable OR and CAO procedures remain part of approval.
data_needed: Applicable evaluation method, permitted materials and trained evaluators
Verified duties, responsibility, qualifications and working conditions
Approved comparator roles and reasoned past decisions
Classification approval and challenge rules
in_practice.logs_to: A restricted evaluation register recording evidence versions, evaluator rationale, approvals and challenges.

evidence.claim: Language models can extract and compare role descriptions, but may confuse polished wording with stronger evidence.
SharePoint version history can preserve the documents used in an evaluation.
The 35% labour saving and 1.3 times end-to-end speedup are untested planning estimates.

risks: Historical classifications may encode inequities that comparator retrieval then repeats.
An eloquent job description may receive more favourable treatment than equivalent work described plainly.
The workflow may use an incompatible or restricted evaluation method.
Use affecting employment terms needs an intended-use assessment under the EU AI Act and applicable AVG safeguards; a nominal approval is insufficient.
research_questions: Which evaluation method applies to each workforce group, and does it permit this form of assistance?
Can evaluators verify actual duties sufficiently well from the available documents?
In blinded trials, do assisted packs improve consistency without changing outcomes because of writing style?
What approval, OR involvement and employee challenge arrangements are required?

tasks.short: Forecast how many permanent and flex workers each site will need.

today.trigger: Annual planning, a seasonal peak forecast or a significant change in expected workload.
steps: Obtain workload forecasts and staffing assumptions from operations.
Establish current employee and agency capacity by site, role and shift.
Estimate future capacity after turnover, absence, leave, hiring and training lead times.
Compare demand and capacity under alternative scenarios.
Agree proposed recruitment and flex requirements with operations and Finance.
systems: Operations planning inputs supplied by site leaders
drudgery: Combining site spreadsheets with different assumptions.
Converting people, contract hours and agency hours into comparable capacity.
Rebuilding seasonal scenarios after each assumption changes.
today.time_sinks: Assumed current workflow: input reconciliation and scenario rebuilding take time. The listed HR systems do not establish workload forecasts, shift rosters or productivity standards.

lenses.faster: Use a repeatable demand-and-capacity model that updates approved inputs and generates site and shift gaps. Remove manual scenario rebuilding and unit conversion.
lenses.autonomous: On each approved planning cycle, rebuild the forecast and publish it when input checks and agreed tolerances pass. Exceptions go to the director; hiring and agency orders require separate approval.
lenses.ambitious: Maintain a rolling forecast that includes the time needed to recruit, train and reach productive capacity. Use it to smooth peak demand and reduce repeated emergency agency requests.
lenses.joy: Remove spreadsheet consolidation and repeated calculations. Keep the discussion with operations about assumptions, resilience and a workable staffing mix.
lenses.options: Compare demand, turnover, absence, productivity and agency-availability scenarios with ranges. Show the cost and service consequences of different permanent and flex mixes.
lenses.altitude: Own the workforce planning assumptions, forecast accuracy and decision thresholds rather than producing each spreadsheet.
reach: Prepare the workforce component of FP&A forecasts.
Give Recruiters and agency coordinators an earlier, approved view of likely demand.

tasks.human_edge: Operations and HR must judge whether assumptions are credible, whether proposed shifts are workable and which staffing risks the company should accept.
tasks.pattern_why: deterministic_software should calculate demand, capacity and scenarios using explicit assumptions; an optional llm_step explains results. A language model should not generate the staffing numbers.

in_practice.trigger: An approved operations forecast or the scheduled workforce planning refresh.
steps: Load approved workload forecasts, employee capacity, recruitment pipeline and agency availability.
Validate units, dates, completeness and reconciliation of people, hours and productive capacity.
Calculate requirements by site, role and shift using agreed productivity and availability assumptions.
Generate scenarios and backtest forecast error; withhold publication when checks fail or thresholds are exceeded.
Publish forecasts that pass the rules and route exceptions for review before any staffing commitment.
in_practice.human_gate: Operations approves demand and productivity assumptions; HR and Finance approve material staffing decisions. Conditional publication covers forecasts only, with no automatic requisitions, agency orders or individual scheduling decisions.
systems: Read-only AFAS Profit, Recruitee and Studytube extracts
data_needed: Operations workload forecasts by site, activity and planning period
Agreed productivity standards, shift constraints and available working hours
Contract hours, aggregate absence and leave assumptions, turnover and start dates
Recruitment lead times, training capacity and valid qualification requirements
Agency hours, availability, rates and historical forecast outcomes
in_practice.logs_to: A restricted forecast register containing input snapshots, assumptions, model version, forecast errors, exceptions and approvals.

evidence.claim: Excel Power Query can repeat structured data preparation for a workforce model.
Explicit demand-and-capacity models can generate reproducible scenarios, but useful accuracy depends on operations data and valid assumptions.
The 55% labour saving and 1.8 times end-to-end speedup are untested planning estimates.

risks: Headcount may be confused with FTE, paid hours or productive hours, especially for 150 to 300 seasonal flex workers.
Missing workload forecasts or unreliable productivity assumptions can make a precise forecast unusable.
A model may assume workers are interchangeable across sites, shifts or certificate requirements.
Forecasts can become self-confirming if hiring is constrained by the forecast and unmet demand is never recorded.
research_questions: Can operations supply reliable workload forecasts and productivity assumptions at the required site and shift detail?
Can employee and agency capacity be reconciled in productive hours without duplicate workers or missing availability?
Does backtesting outperform a simple seasonal baseline at the lead times needed for hiring and training?
What error and data-quality thresholds justify automatic forecast publication?

role.altitude: The HR Director becomes the owner of a people operating system: clear service rules, reliable evidence, accountable decisions and measurable improvement from vacancy to productive employment at day 90.
reach: Prepare first-pass people analysis and request specialist validation from the People Analytics and HRIS Analyst.
Develop workforce and HR spending scenarios with FP&A and the Controller.
Coordinate cross-site onboarding and training capacity with operations and Learning and Development.
Prepare policy and role evaluation evidence for HR Business Partners and Compensation and Benefits.
Lead a shared HR and operations programme to improve productive 90-day hires.
role.ceiling_note: The eight tasks total 1,364.1 hours annually, about 85% of the implied 1,600-hour role. The illustrative labour savings total about 557 hours, or 35% of the whole role, before setup, maintenance, overlap and additional review; the unlisted 236 hours are unestimated. At EUR 110/hour, that is roughly EUR 61,200 of gross capacity value, not a cash saving. Speedup estimates include preparation and review, while consultation, negotiations and statutory timelines still limit elapsed time. Trust, sensitive employee decisions and leadership remain substantial human work.
skills_to_grow: Define vacancy cohorts, productivity criteria and 90-day outcomes without rewarding metric gaming.
Challenge data quality, uncertainty and causal claims.
Design access controls, retention rules and proportionate AVG safeguards.
